approved: Treasury Laws Amendment (Making Sure Every State and Territory Gets Their Fair Share of GST) Bill 2018
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
This bill changes how the GST is shared among states and territories so the system is fairer.

It moves from full equalisation to reasonable equalisation based on New South Wales and Victoria, introduces a minimum GST relativity floor set by the Treasurer, and adds extra Commonwealth money to the GST pool permanently.
Short-term payments are provided to states or territories with a GST relativity below 0.7 and to the Northern Territory if its relativity falls below its 2017-18 factor.
The bill transitions horizontal fiscal equalisation from full to reasonable equalisation.
It introduces a minimum GST relativity floor that the Treasurer may set for any state or territory.
It permanently boosts the GST revenue pool with extra Commonwealth financial assistance.
States and territories that receive GST revenue shares.

The Treasury Laws Amendment (Making Sure Every State and Territory Gets Their Fair Share of GST) Bill 2018 reforms GST distribution to provide a fairer and more sustainable system, leaving all states better off. Key measures include a new equalisation benchmark based on the stronger of New South Wales or Victoria, a permanent relativity floor of 0.7 rising to 0.75, and Commonwealth cash injections of $600 million in 2021-22 and $250 million in 2024-25, indexed annually, with an additional $9 billion over 10 years to 2028-29.

Labor supported the Treasury Laws Amendment (Making Sure Every State and Territory Gets Their Fair Share of GST) Bill 2018, which guarantees a GST floor for all states and territories and ensures no state is worse off, after the government backflipped on its earlier opposition; Western Australia had received as low as 30 cents per dollar of GST revenue.

The bill transitions the GST distribution system from full fiscal equalisation to a benchmark based on the stronger of New South Wales or Victoria, implemented over eight years in three steps, with no state or territory left worse off. It guarantees a minimum GST relativity floor of 70c then 75c per dollar, provides an additional $9 billion in Commonwealth funding over 10 years and $1 billion extra annually from 2026-27, and addresses Western Australia’s drop to 30c in the dollar.
